title: console: the settings page asks a toggle's confirmOffText before it saves the toggle turned off (ruling A on #30418, the domain:ui half)
body:
domain:spec#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzfgvGexKn9vLHsy89K

Filing gate: executing a recorded ruling. The maintainer ruled A on #30418 (6657805240), bind (4): "The console's settings page honours it before save (the `domain:ui` half; the renderer's ignored `confirmText` on `action_button` stays on its own card)." The spec half is PR #30489 (#30418). ⛔ Not a claim. Suggested-grade: p1, the reader of a new protocol key (Prime Directive #10: a declared key with no reader is a silent no-op). Route: `domain:ui`.

## What happens today

Once PR #30489 lands, a settings-manifest toggle specifier may declare `confirmOffText: I18nLabel` ("confirm dialog text shown before a toggle's value changes to off; omit = no confirm"), and `auth.manifest.ts` declares it on `email_password_enabled` with "people who sign in with a password will need another way in". The console's settings page (`apps/console/src/pages/settings/`, `SettingsField.tsx`, `useSettingsLabel.ts`) does not read the key, so Setup still turns email and password sign-in off without asking (#30299).

## Wanted

- [ ] When a toggle whose specifier declares `confirmOffText` is changed from on to off, the settings page shows a confirm dialog with that text before the value is saved; cancel leaves the toggle on and saves nothing. Turning it on asks nothing.
- [ ] The text resolves through the same translation path as the toggle's other labels (`settings.<ns>.keys.<key>.confirmOffText`, falling back to the manifest literal).
- [ ] A toggle without the key behaves exactly as today.
- [ ] Tests: confirm shown and cancel keeps the value; confirm accepted saves; no key, no dialog. A browser check on Setup's authentication page for `email_password_enabled`.

Not in scope: the ignored `confirmText` on `action_button` handlers (its own card). The #30202 server floor.
